name: Pain and fear during procedures in children
summary: Children undergoing short but painful procedures experience distress that sedation cannot always address, and fear compounds the pain itself.
sourceNote: Cited study compares distraction during closed reduction in children. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the challenge.

name: Severe acute pain where drug options are limited
summary: In crises such as vaso-occlusive episodes, pain is severe and escalating analgesia carries its own risks, leaving a gap for non-pharmacological adjuncts.
sourceNote: Cited study examines headset use during severe crisis pain. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the challenge.

name: Keeping patients engaged in home-based programmes
summary: Multi-week self-directed therapy works only if patients keep going after the first fortnight, and drop-off is the usual outcome.
sourceNote: Cited review traces implementation considerations for a home-delivered programme. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the challenge.

name: Running simulation at cohort scale
summary: A scenario that works for six learners rarely survives contact with a cohort of three hundred, once headset supply, cleaning, and timetabling are counted.
sourceNote: Cited work discusses implications for health professions education at scale. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the challenge.

name: How much realism a scenario actually needs
summary: Higher fidelity costs more and is assumed to teach better, but which cues change behaviour — and which are decoration — is rarely tested.
sourceNote: Cited controlled trial isolates one sensory cue and measures its effect on safety behaviour. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the challenge.

name: Rehearsing emergencies too rare to schedule
summary: The events that most need practice — outbreaks, mass casualties, rare deteriorations — are precisely the ones a rota cannot produce on demand.
sourceLabel: International Journal of Qualitative Studies on Health and Well-being
sourceNote: Cited study explores nurses' experience of simulated infectious-disease response. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the challenge.

name: Building manual skill without theatre or cadaver access
summary: Procedural competence needs repetition, but theatre time, cadaveric material, and supervision are all scarce and unevenly distributed.
sourceNote: Cited work describes an assisted system for teaching a manual shaping skill. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the challenge.

name: Assessing technique without a supervisor in the room
summary: Competence is still largely judged by observation, which is expensive, inconsistent between assessors, and hard to schedule.
sourceLabel: International Journal of Nursing Studies Advances
sourceNote: Cited cohort study measures learning curves for a clinical skill. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the challenge.

name: Regaining arm function after stroke
summary: Recovery needs many repetitions of movement that is difficult, tiring, and unrewarding to perform, so adherence and intensity both suffer.
sourceNote: Cited trial studies repetitive simulation circuit training for post-stroke arm weakness. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the challenge.

name: Translating motor-learning research into therapy
summary: Findings about how movement is relearned are well established in the laboratory and slow to reach the treatment room.
sourceNote: Cited paper proposes a network-oriented approach to neurorehabilitation after stroke. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the challenge.

name: Supervising therapy that happens at home
summary: Moving therapy into the home removes travel but also removes the clinician, leaving technique uncorrected and progress unmeasured.
sourceNote: Cited trial evaluates a mixed-reality rehabilitation programme delivered outside the clinic. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the challenge.

name: Fitting immersive sessions into a full curriculum
summary: Every proposal adds teaching to a saturated timetable; the harder question is what comes out, and how that is defended to faculty.
sourceNote: Cited synthesis reviews active-learning approaches in health professions education. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the challenge.

name: Training psychological first aid at scale
summary: Demand for responders spikes exactly when trainers are least available, and conventional courses do not scale to meet it.
sourceNote: Cited work explores scalable delivery of psychological first aid training. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the challenge.

name: Keeping the plan visible during the operation
summary: A plan built from imaging has to be carried into theatre and aligned with the patient on the table, where attention and sterile field both constrain how it can be shown.
sourceNote: Cited clearance record describes a mixed-reality spine navigation device. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the challenge.

name: Turning imaging into a usable model in time
summary: Interactive three-dimensional models are compelling in demonstration; producing one for an urgent case depends on segmentation staffing, not software.
sourceNote: Cited clearance record describes a surgical visualization viewer. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the challenge.

name: Aligning a 3D model to the patient on the table
summary: An augmented overlay is only useful if it sits exactly where the anatomy is. Registration has to survive patient movement, soft-tissue shift, and a surgeon's changing viewpoint, and the error budget is millimetres.
sourceLabel: Cureus — AR in Spine Surgery: a narrative review
sourceNote: Cited review covers clinical accuracy, workflow efficiency, and the barriers still limiting adoption. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the difficulty.

name: Recreating what tissue actually feels like
summary: Visual realism has advanced far faster than touch. Without convincing resistance and texture, a simulator teaches the sequence of a procedure but not the feel of it, which is much of the skill.
sourceLabel: Smart haptic gloves for VR surgery simulation (pilot study)
sourceNote: Cited pilot study evaluates haptic gloves for neurosurgical drain training and discusses the fidelity gap. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the difficulty.

name: Latency quietly degrades fine motor precision
summary: Delay between hand and image is tolerable when watching, but not when operating. Small amounts of lag measurably reduce precision and raise cognitive load, and the effect compounds the longer someone works.
sourceLabel: Scientific Reports — visual-haptic latency and fine motor performance
sourceNote: Cited study measures how haptic feedback and visual-haptic latency affect performance on a laparoscopic task. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the difficulty.

name: Knowing whether an in-headset score means anything
summary: Headsets record rich data — gaze, movement, timing — and it is tempting to treat it as assessment. Establishing that those numbers correspond to real clinical ability is a separate and harder task.
sourceLabel: arXiv — Cognitive Assessment and Training in Extended Reality
sourceNote: Cited survey reviews multimodal XR assessment systems, clinical utility, and open challenges. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the difficulty.

name: Building once and running on every headset
summary: Hardware turns over faster than clinical software can be revalidated. Without a portable target, each new device risks a rebuild — a serious cost when the software is a regulated medical product.
sourceNote: The OpenXR standard exists specifically to address cross-device fragmentation; the specification page sets out the scope of that problem. The problem statement is AVRMD's framing; the cited work documents the difficulty.
